wines: Chablis or unoaked Chardonnay — mineral, lemon, no heavy oak so the fish stays delicate
Muscadet or Pinot Grigio — high acid, light body, a squeeze of citrus on the finish
Albariño if the bake has herbs or a little garlic
beers: Bright Pilsner or Kölsch — clean malt, enough snap to cut butter
Witbier with citrus peel if the pan sauce is lemon-caper
sides: Steamed new potatoes with parsley and olive oil
A simple green salad with a sharp vinaigrette
vegetables: Asparagus or broccolini, quickly roasted so it stays green
Sautéed spinach or French beans with lemon zest
Fennel, shaved or gently braised — sweet, anise, lovely with white wine
entries.notes: Flounder is lean and mild. Keep the glass light, the vegetables bright, and skip heavy reds unless the guest insists on a chilled, low-tannin Pinot.

wines: Pinot Noir — light tannin, cherry, a classic with richer fish
Dry Rosé or a textured white Burgundy if they prefer white
beers: Session IPA if the glaze is citrus or spicy
entries.notes: Salmon can take a little more body than flounder. Pinot or Rosé keeps pace without fighting the oil.

wines: Cabernet Sauvignon — cassis, structure, at home with char
Malbec or a bold red blend if they want something rounder
beers: House Porter — roasted malt, a little chocolate, loves a sear
IPA if they want bitterness against the fat
sides: A peppercorn or chimichurri on the side
entries.notes: Match intensity: char and fat want tannin or roast. Keep a lighter lager as a polite backup.

wines: Chardonnay with a little texture
Dry Riesling if herbs and lemon lead
entries.notes: Roast chicken is a canvas — follow the seasoning. Herb-lemon wants Riesling; browned butter wants Chardonnay.

wines: Pinot Noir
Off-dry Riesling with a glaze
entries.notes: Pork likes a hint of fruit and spice — not a heavy Cabernet unless it's a smoked shoulder.

wines: Chianti or Sangiovese with tomato
Pinot Grigio with cream or seafood
sides: Garlic bread only if they ask
entries.notes: Follow the sauce, not the noodle.

wines: Muscadet
Champagne or dry sparkling
vegetables: A few raw radishes on the side — palate reset
entries.notes: Stay razor-dry and saline. No oak, no sweetness.

wines: Zinfandel or a juicy red blend
Chilled Gamay if they want lighter
entries.notes: Fat and bun want either snap (lager) or fruit (Zin). Keep one of each in mind.

wines: Syrah or Grenache
Bordeaux if rosemary and garlic lead
sides: Mint yogurt if they like cool contrast
entries.notes: Lamb's sweetness loves pepper and herb — Syrah is the easy first pour.

wines: Sauvignon Blanc
Dry Rosé
vegetables: The salad is the vegetable — add herbs, not cream
entries.notes: Vinaigrette wants acid in the glass. Skip oaky Chardonnay.
